title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood

reading.body:
This incident shows an impersonation scheme in which scammers sent emails pretending to be Terry Gross and other named staff of a well-known public radio program. The emails were personalized, referencing each target's specific work and proposing relevant interview topics, before eventually requesting a fee for production costs. Cybersecurity experts cited in the reporting attribute the convincing personalization to AI tools, which allowed the messages to move beyond the generic phrasing typical of older scam attempts.

The failure is not one of a deployed AI system acting on its own, but of AI being used as a tool by human actors to lower the cost and raise the quality of fraud. The AI component sat at the content-generation stage, producing individualized text at scale. No organizational safeguard, such as a verification step built into legitimate booking processes, existed on the scammer's side by design, and targets had no in-band signal to distinguish the fake outreach from a genuine inquiry.

It is not established who is responsible for sending the emails, that any individual has been charged or convicted, or that any specific AI product was used to generate the messages.

reports.title: ‘Too good to be true?’: No, WHYY’s Terry Gross did not personally email you to be a guest on ‘Fresh Air’
Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood

summary:
Scammers are using personalized emails that impersonate Terry Gross and other staff members from WHYY's "Fresh Air" radio show to defraud potential guests. The emails include detailed references to recipients' work and propose interview topics, making them appear legitimate. Targets are eventually asked to pay fees, typically $250, for supposed production costs. Several authors, entertainers and public figures have reported receiving these messages, with some emails sent from addresses like "terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com."

WHYY, NPR and the "Fresh Air" program have confirmed they are investigating the scam and working with law enforcement. According to cybersecurity experts, artificial intelligence has made such impersonation attempts much more convincing and personalized than traditional scams. WHYY stated it never charges guests for interviews and advised recipients to verify any interview requests through legitimate contact methods rather than responding to suspicious emails.
